items.q: Crumpled tissue paper cytoplasm macrophages with massive splenomegaly and Erlenmeyer flask femurs indicate which disease?
items.exp: Gaucher cells are glucocerebroside laden macrophages with fibrillary crumpled cytoplasm expanding spleen, liver and marrow, remodelling femurs into flask shapes. Glucocerebrosidase assay confirms.
r: Incorrect. Niemann Pick foam cells store sphingomyelin with neurodegeneration.
Correct. Crumpled paper cells mean Gaucher disease.
Incorrect. Tay Sachs spares organs and targets neurons.
Incorrect. Hurler stores glycosaminoglycans with coarse facies.
items.kp: Crumpled paper macrophage equals Gaucher cell.

items.q: Infant developmental regression, exaggerated startle and cherry red spot WITHOUT organomegaly indicate what?
items.exp: Hexosaminidase A deficiency stores GM2 only in neurons, causing regression and cherry red spot (stored ganglion cells around normal fovea) without visceral enlargement, unlike Niemann Pick.
r: Incorrect. Niemann Pick adds hepatosplenomegaly.
Correct. Neurons only, no big organs: Tay Sachs.
Incorrect. Gaucher type 2 has organomegaly with neurology.
Incorrect. Leukodystrophy causes white matter regression differently.
items.kp: Cherry red plus small organs equals Tay Sachs.

items.q: Floppy infant with huge hypertrophic heart and elevated CK from acid maltase deficiency has what?
items.exp: Pompe disease (acid alpha glucosidase, lysosomal) stores glycogen in heart and skeletal muscle causing infantile hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, hypotonia and early death without enzyme replacement.
r: Incorrect. Von Gierke hits liver glucose release instead.
Correct. Lysosomal glycogen in heart and muscle is Pompe.
Incorrect. McArdle causes exercise intolerance in older patients.
Incorrect. Cori (debrancher) causes milder liver muscle disease.
items.kp: Pompe is glycogen storage that behaves like lysosomal disease.

items.q: Fasting hypoglycaemia, huge liver, lactic acidosis and doll like facies in an infant suggest which enzyme loss?
items.exp: Von Gierke disease blocks the final common step of glycogenolysis and gluconeogenesis, so fasting causes hypoglycaemia with lactate, uric acid and lipid elevation plus hepatomegaly from stored glycogen and fat.
r: Incorrect. That loss causes Pompe cardiomuscular disease.
Correct. Glucose 6 phosphatase loss is von Gierke disease.
Incorrect. Muscle enzyme loss spares fasting glucose.
Incorrect. Branching loss (Andersen) causes cirrhosis pattern.
items.kp: Cannot release glucose at all: von Gierke fasting crisis.

items.q: Exercise induced cramps improving after brief rest (second wind) with myoglobinuria indicate which glycogen disease?
items.exp: McArdle muscle cannot mobilise its glycogen, cramping early in exercise until blood borne fuels arrive (second wind), with rhabdomyolysis dark urine after intense effort. Flat venous lactate rise on exercise testing supports it.
r: Incorrect. Pompe weakens constantly with heart disease.
Correct. Second wind phenomenon means McArdle disease.
Incorrect. Von Gierke is hepatic fasting disease of infants.
Incorrect. Hers (liver phosphorylase) is milder hepatic disease.
items.kp: Second wind after cramps is pathognomonic McArdle talk.

items.q: Coarse facies, corneal clouding, stiff joints and intellectual decline in a toddler suggest which storage group?
items.exp: Hurler syndrome (alpha L iduronidase) stores dermatan and heparan sulfate producing coarse features, clouded corneas, dysostosis multiplex and cognitive decline. Urine glycosaminoglycans screen the group.
r: Incorrect. Glycogen diseases centre on liver, heart or muscle energy.
Correct. Glycosaminoglycan storage causes this phenotype.
Incorrect. Neuronal sphingolipid disease lacks coarse somatic features.
Incorrect. Peroxisomal disease causes leukodystrophy and liver signs differently.
items.kp: Coarse plus cloudy cornea equals mucopolysaccharide storage.

items.q: Hunter syndrome differs from Hurler syndrome most testably how?
o: X linked inheritance with clear corneas
items.exp: Hunter (iduronate sulfatase) is X linked affecting boys, with clear corneas despite similar coarse features, while Hurler is recessive with corneal clouding. This pair is a perennial exam contrast.
r: Incorrect. Hurler is recessive; Hunter is X linked recessive.
Correct. X linked plus clear corneas means Hunter.
Incorrect. Dysostosis occurs in both syndromes.
Incorrect. Both store glycosaminoglycans, not glycogen.
items.kp: Clear cornea in a Hurler like boy: Hunter syndrome.

items.q: Fabry disease (alpha galactosidase A, X linked) characteristically causes which pain pattern?
o: Burning acral pain crises (acroparesthesia) with angiokeratomas
Pain only after exercise with second wind
items.exp: Fabry stores globotriaosylceramide in vessels, nerves, kidney and heart causing burning hand foot pain crises, angiokeratoma bathing trunk lesions, renal failure and cardiomyopathy. Enzyme therapy exists, so recognition matters.
r: Incorrect. Large joint destruction suggests other storage or arthritis.
Correct. Acral burning pain plus angiokeratomas means Fabry.
Incorrect. Second wind belongs to McArdle disease.
Incorrect. Gaucher bone pain is deep and crisis like, not acral burning.
items.kp: Burning hands and feet in a boy: do not miss Fabry disease.

items.q: Metachromatic leukodystrophy from arylsulfatase A deficiency damages mainly what tissue?
o: Central and peripheral myelin (leukodystrophy with neuropathy)
items.exp: Sulfatide storage destroys myelin centrally (regression, white matter disease) and peripherally (neuropathy with slow conduction), combining upper and lower motor signs that localise the diagnosis.
r: Incorrect. Liver is not the target organ here.
Correct. Myelin central plus peripheral is the signature.
Incorrect. Heart is spared characteristically.
Incorrect. Kidneys are not primary targets.
items.kp: Regression plus peripheral neuropathy equals metachromatic disease pattern.

items.q: Why does enzyme replacement help Gaucher viscera more than Tay Sachs brain?
o: Intravenous enzyme crosses blood brain barrier poorly and neurons are already lost
Tay Sachs enzyme is too large to infuse
items.exp: Recombinant enzymes reach reticuloendothelial organs via mannose receptors but cross the blood brain barrier negligibly, and lost neurons cannot regenerate, so neuronal storage diseases need other strategies started presymptomatically.
r: Incorrect. Purity is not the limiting factor.
Correct. Barrier exclusion plus neuronal loss limits brain benefit.
Incorrect. Gaucher stores are intracellular lysosomal too.
Incorrect. Infusion size is not the stated barrier.
items.kp: Enzyme in blood does not equal enzyme in brain.
